description:
I'm a software engineer with three years of experience building things end-to-end — backend APIs, data pipelines, cloud infrastructure, and the React frontends that tie it all together. Most of my work has lived in Java and Spring Boot, though I've picked up Python, Node.js, and a healthy appreciation for distributed systems along the way.
Lately I've been drawn to the intersection of AI and practical tooling — which led me to build Dzigned, a portfolio generator that uses LLMs to turn a resume into a deployed website in minutes.

description: Built the backend services that kept a recruitment platform running candidate intake, role-matching, and the APIs that tied everything together with third-party tools like ATS, email, and calendar systems.
Crossed into frontend too, building React dashboards that gave recruiters and account managers a clear view of their pipeline without having to dig through raw data.
Handled the database side as well designing schemas for candidates, requisitions, and placements, and contributing to the Docker and AWS pipelines that kept deployments boring in the best way.
Worked across the full stack of a multi-tenant SaaS platform — Django and Spring Boot on the backend, React and TypeScript on the frontend, GraphQL APIs connecting everything in between.

Built the data pipelines that kept HubSpot and QuickBooks in sync for multiple clients — normalization, unified storage, cross-tenant security the kind of plumbing that has to work quietly or everyone notices.

Wired in GPT-4 so business owners could just ask questions about their data in plain English instead of waiting on manual reports. Also handled the Kubernetes and Helm deployments that kept all of this running without drama.
Built Node.js and Spring Boot microservices for PepsiCo's internal platform the kind of system that quietly serves thousands of retail locations and only gets noticed when something breaks.
Designed a ticketing system with automated assignment and escalation logic that took the manual triage burden off distributed ops teams less firefighting, more actual work getting done.
Handled the Kafka side too producers and consumers moving store alerts and ticket events across multiple downstream services, plus the PostgreSQL and MongoDB schemas underneath all of it.

items.description:
Built this one end-to-end, Spring Boot backend, React frontend, MongoDB and PostgreSQL underneath, Gemini API doing the heavy lifting on style generation. The kind of project where you end up solving problems you didn't know existed when you started.
Upload your resume, review the pre-filled portfolio, pick an AI-generated style, and publish straight to GitHub Pages via OAuth. The whole flow that used to take hours now takes minutes.

Trained a GAN with a U-Net generator and PatchGAN discriminator to reconstruct sharp images from motion-blurred inputs — the kind of problem that sounds simple until you're debugging why your generator keeps producing grey blobs.
Experimented with perceptual loss functions, learning-rate scheduling, and data augmentation to push image quality further than standard pixel-wise loss alone would allow.

Built an end-to-end pipeline that takes an image and generates a natural language caption CNN encoder to extract visual features, transformer-based decoder to turn those features into coherent sentences.
Fine-tuned on a standard captioning dataset and spent a good amount of time on beam search and caption diversity, because "a dog" is technically correct but not very interesting.
